answer: An agent network mitigates Sybil attacks by routing trust across a peer-to-peer trellis of bilateral credit vouchers. New identities require peer endorsement, forcing an attacker to commit scarce capital to forge incoming credit channels rather than spawning costless virtual nodes. Unendorsed adversaries are trapped on an economic island, unable to route payments through honest participants. However, rigid credit caps can throttle transaction throughput during sudden volume surges.
